paragraphs.text: And straightway in the morning the chief priests with the elders and scribes, and the whole council, held a consultation, and bound Jesus, and carried him away, and delivered him up to Pilate.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εὐθὺς πρωῒ συμβούλιον ποιήσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς μετὰ τῶν πρεσβυτέρων καὶ γραμματέων καὶ ὅλον τὸ συνέδριον δήσαντες τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἀπήνεγκαν καὶ παρέδωκαν Πιλάτῳ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai euthys prōi symboulion poiēsantes hoi archiereis meta tōn presbyterōn kai grammateōn kai holon to synedrion dēsantes ton Iēsoun apēnenkan kai paredōkan Pilatō.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate asked him, Art thou the King of the Jews? And he answering saith unto him, Thou sayest.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Σὺ εἶ ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων; ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς αὐτῷ λέγει· Σὺ λέγεις.
paragraphs.translit: kai epērōtēsen auton ho Pilatos· Sy ei ho basileus tōn Ioudaiōn; ho de apokritheis autō legei· Sy legeis.

paragraphs.text: And the chief priests accused him of many things.
paragraphs.original: καὶ κατηγόρουν αὐτοῦ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς πολλά.
paragraphs.translit: kai katēgoroun autou hoi archiereis polla.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate again asked him, saying, Answerest thou nothing? behold how many things they accuse thee of.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος πάλιν ἐπηρώτα αὐτὸν λέγων· Οὐκ ἀποκρίνῃ οὐδέν; ἴδε πόσα σου κατηγοροῦσιν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Pilatos palin epērōta auton legōn· Ouk apokrinē ouden; ide posa sou katēgorousin.

paragraphs.text: But Jesus no more answered anything; insomuch that Pilate marvelled.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς οὐκέτι οὐδὲν ἀπεκρίθη, ὥστε θαυμάζειν τὸν Πιλᾶτον.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous ouketi ouden apekrithē, hōste thaumazein ton Pilaton.

paragraphs.text: Now at the feast he used to release unto them one prisoner, whom they asked of him.
paragraphs.original: Κατὰ δὲ ἑορτὴν ἀπέλυεν αὐτοῖς ἕνα δέσμιον ὃν παρῃτοῦντο.
paragraphs.translit: Kata de heortēn apelyen autois hena desmion hon parētounto.

paragraphs.text: And there was one called Barabbas, [lying] bound with them that had made insurrection, men who in the insurrection had committed murder.
paragraphs.original: ἦν δὲ ὁ λεγόμενος Βαραββᾶς μετὰ τῶν στασιαστῶν δεδεμένος οἵτινες ἐν τῇ στάσει φόνον πεποιήκεισαν.
paragraphs.translit: ēn de ho legomenos Barabbas meta tōn stasiastōn dedemenos hoitines en tē stasei phonon pepoiēkeisan.

paragraphs.text: And the multitude went up and began to ask him [to do] as he was wont to do unto them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀναβὰς ὁ ὄχλος ἤρξατο αἰτεῖσθαι καθὼς ἐποίει αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: kai anabas ho ochlos ērxato aiteisthai kathōs epoiei autois.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate answered them, saying, Will ye that I release unto you the King of the Jews?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς λέγων· Θέλετε ἀπολύσω ὑμῖν τὸν βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων;
paragraphs.translit: ho de Pilatos apekrithē autois legōn· Thelete apolysō hymin ton basilea tōn Ioudaiōn;

paragraphs.text: For he perceived that for envy the chief priests had delivered him up.
paragraphs.original: ἐγίνωσκεν γὰρ ὅτι διὰ φθόνον παραδεδώκεισαν αὐτὸν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς.
paragraphs.translit: eginōsken gar hoti dia phthonon paradedōkeisan auton hoi archiereis.

paragraphs.text: But the chief priests stirred up the multitude, that he should rather release Barabbas unto them.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ἀρχιερεῖς ἀνέσεισαν τὸν ὄχλον ἵνα μᾶλλον τὸν Βαραββᾶν ἀπολύσῃ αὐτοῖς.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de archiereis aneseisan ton ochlon hina mallon ton Barabban apolysē autois.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate again answered and said unto them, What then shall I do unto him whom ye call the King of the Jews?
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος πάλιν ἀποκριθεὶς ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Τί οὖν θέλετε ποιήσω ὃν λέγετε τὸν βασιλέα τῶν Ἰουδαίων;
paragraphs.translit: ho de Pilatos palin apokritheis elegen autois· Ti oun thelete poiēsō hon legete ton basilea tōn Ioudaiōn;

paragraphs.text: And they cried out again, Crucify him.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ πάλιν ἔκραξαν· Σταύρωσον αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de palin ekraxan· Staurōson auton.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate said unto them, Why, what evil hath he done? But they cried out exceedingly, Crucify him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς· Τί γὰρ ἐποίησεν κακόν; οἱ δὲ περισσῶς ἔκραξαν· Σταύρωσον αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Pilatos elegen autois· Ti gar epoiēsen kakon; hoi de perissōs ekraxan· Staurōson auton.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate, wishing to content the multitude, released unto them Barabbas, and delivered Jesus, when he had scourged him, to be crucified.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος βουλόμενος τῷ ὄχλῳ τὸ ἱκανὸν ποιῆσαι ἀπέλυσεν αὐτοῖς τὸν Βαραββᾶν, καὶ παρέδωκεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν φραγελλώσας ἵνα σταυρωθῇ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Pilatos boulomenos tō ochlō to hikanon poiēsai apelysen autois ton Barabban, kai paredōken ton Iēsoun phragellōsas hina staurōthē.

paragraphs.text: And the soldiers led him away within the court, which is the Praetorium; and they call together the whole band.
paragraphs.original: Οἱ δὲ στρατιῶται ἀπήγαγον αὐτὸν ἔσω τῆς αὐλῆς, ὅ ἐστιν πραιτώριον, καὶ συγκαλοῦσιν ὅλην τὴν σπεῖραν.
paragraphs.translit: Hoi de stratiōtai apēgagon auton esō tēs aulēs, ho estin praitōrion, kai synkalousin holēn tēn speiran.

paragraphs.text: And they clothe him with purple, and platting a crown of thorns, they put it on him;
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐνδιδύσκουσιν αὐτὸν πορφύραν καὶ περιτιθέασιν αὐτῷ πλέξαντες ἀκάνθινον στέφανον·
paragraphs.translit: kai endidyskousin auton porphyran kai perititheasin autō plexantes akanthinon stephanon·

paragraphs.text: and they began to salute him, Hail, King of the Jews!
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἤρξαντο ἀσπάζεσθαι αὐτόν· Χαῖρε, βασιλεῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων·
paragraphs.translit: kai ērxanto aspazesthai auton· Chaire, basileu tōn Ioudaiōn·

paragraphs.text: And they smote his head with a reed, and spat upon him, and bowing their knees worshipped him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἔτυπτον αὐτοῦ τὴν κεφαλὴν καλάμῳ καὶ ἐνέπτυον αὐτῷ, καὶ τιθέντες τὰ γόνατα προσεκύνουν αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: kai etypton autou tēn kephalēn kalamō kai eneptyon autō, kai tithentes ta gonata prosekynoun autō.

paragraphs.text: And when they had mocked him, they took off from him the purple, and put on him his garments. And they lead him out to crucify him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ὅτε ἐνέπαιξαν αὐτῷ, ἐξέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὴν πορφύραν καὶ ἐνέδυσαν αὐτὸν τὰ ἱμάτια τὰ ἴδια. καὶ ἐξάγουσιν αὐτὸν ἵνα σταυρώσωσιν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: kai hote enepaixan autō, exedysan auton tēn porphyran kai enedysan auton ta himatia ta idia. kai exagousin auton hina staurōsōsin auton.

paragraphs.text: And they compel one passing by, Simon of Cyrene, coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to go [with them], that he might bear his cross.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀγγαρεύουσιν παράγοντά τινα Σίμωνα Κυρηναῖον ἐρχόμενον ἀπʼ ἀγροῦ, τὸν πατέρα Ἀλεξάνδρου καὶ Ῥούφου, ἵνα ἄρῃ τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: Kai angareuousin paragonta tina Simōna Kyrēnaion erchomenon apʼ agrou, ton patera Alexandrou kai Rhouphou, hina arē ton stauron autou.

paragraphs.text: And they bring him unto the place Golgotha, which is, being interpreted, The place of a skull.
paragraphs.original: καὶ φέρουσιν αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τὸν Γολγοθᾶν τόπον, ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Κρανίου Τόπος.
paragraphs.translit: kai pherousin auton epi ton Golgothan topon, ho estin methermēneuomenon Kraniou Topos.

paragraphs.text: And they offered him wine mingled with myrrh: but he received it not.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐδίδουν αὐτῷ ἐσμυρνισμένον οἶνον, ὃς δὲ οὐκ ἔλαβεν.
paragraphs.translit: kai edidoun autō esmyrnismenon oinon, hos de ouk elaben.

paragraphs.text: And they crucify him, and part his garments among them, casting lots upon them, what each should take.
paragraphs.original: καὶ σταυροῦσιν αὐτὸν καὶ διαμερίζονται τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ, βάλλοντες κλῆρον ἐπʼ αὐτὰ τίς τί ἄρῃ.
paragraphs.translit: kai staurousin auton kai diamerizontai ta himatia autou, ballontes klēron epʼ auta tis ti arē.

paragraphs.text: And it was the third hour, and they crucified him.
paragraphs.original: Ἦν δὲ ὥρα τρίτη καὶ ἐσταύρωσαν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Ēn de hōra tritē kai estaurōsan auton.

paragraphs.text: And the superscription of his accusation was written over, THE KING OF THE JEWS.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἦν ἡ ἐπιγραφὴ τῆς αἰτίας αὐτοῦ ἐπιγεγραμμένη· Ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.
paragraphs.translit: kai ēn hē epigraphē tēs aitias autou epigegrammenē· Ho basileus tōn Ioudaiōn.

paragraphs.text: And with him they crucify two robbers; one on his right hand, and one on his left.
paragraphs.original: καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ σταυροῦσιν δύο λῃστάς, ἕνα ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ ἕνα ἐξ εὐωνύμων αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: kai syn autō staurousin dyo lēstas, hena ek dexiōn kai hena ex euōnymōn autou.

paragraphs.text: [And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, And he was reckoned with transgressors.]
And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ha! Thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ οἱ παραπορευόμενοι ἐβλασφήμουν αὐτὸν κινοῦντες τὰς κεφαλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ λέγοντες· Οὐὰ ὁ καταλύων τὸν ναὸν καὶ οἰκοδομῶν ἐν τρισὶν ἡμέραις,
paragraphs.translit: Kai hoi paraporeuomenoi eblasphēmoun auton kinountes tas kephalas autōn kai legontes· Oua ho katalyōn ton naon kai oikodomōn en trisin hēmerais,

paragraphs.text: save thyself, and come down from the cross.
paragraphs.original: σῶσον σεαυτὸν καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ.
paragraphs.translit: sōson seauton katabas apo tou staurou.

paragraphs.text: In like manner also the chief priests mocking [him] among themselves with the scribes said, He saved others; himself he cannot save.
paragraphs.original: ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς ἐμπαίζοντες πρὸς ἀλλήλους μετὰ τῶν γραμματέων ἔλεγον· Ἄλλους ἔσωσεν, ἑαυτὸν οὐ δύναται σῶσαι·
paragraphs.translit: homoiōs kai hoi archiereis empaizontes pros allēlous meta tōn grammateōn elegon· Allous esōsen, heauton ou dynatai sōsai·

paragraphs.text: Let the Christ, the King of Israel, now come down from the cross, that we may see and believe. And they that were crucified with him reproached him.
paragraphs.original: ὁ χριστὸς ὁ βασιλεὺς Ἰσραὴλ καταβάτω νῦν ἀπὸ τοῦ σταυροῦ, ἵνα ἴδωμεν καὶ πιστεύσωμεν. καὶ οἱ συνεσταυρωμένοι σὺν αὐτῷ ὠνείδιζον αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: ho christos ho basileus Israēl katabatō nyn apo tou staurou, hina idōmen kai pisteusōmen. kai hoi synestaurōmenoi syn autō ōneidizon auton.

paragraphs.text: And when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ γενομένης ὥρας ἕκτης σκότος ἐγένετο ἐφʼ ὅλην τὴν γῆν ἕως ὥρας ἐνάτης.
paragraphs.translit: Kai genomenēs hōras hektēs skotos egeneto ephʼ holēn tēn gēn heōs hōras enatēs.

paragraphs.text: And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
paragraphs.original: καὶ τῇ ἐνάτῃ ὥρᾳ ἐβόησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Ἐλωῒ ἐλωῒ λεμὰ σαβαχθάνι; ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον Ὁ θεός μου ὁ θεός μου, εἰς τί ἐγκατέλιπές με;
paragraphs.translit: kai tē enatē hōra eboēsen ho Iēsous phōnē megalē· Elōi elōi lema sabachthani; ho estin methermēneuomenon Ho theos mou ho theos mou, eis ti enkatelipes me;

paragraphs.text: And some of them that stood by, when they heard it, said, Behold, he calleth Elijah.
paragraphs.original: καί τινες τῶν παρεστηκότων ἀκούσαντες ἔλεγον· Ἴδε Ἠλίαν φωνεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: kai tines tōn parestēkotōn akousantes elegon· Ide Ēlian phōnei.

paragraphs.text: And one ran, and filling a sponge full of vinegar, put it on a reed, and gave him to drink, saying, Let be; let us see whether Elijah cometh to take him down.
paragraphs.original: δραμὼν δέ τις καὶ γεμίσας σπόγγον ὄξους περιθεὶς καλάμῳ ἐπότιζεν αὐτόν, λέγων· Ἄφετε ἴδωμεν εἰ ἔρχεται Ἠλίας καθελεῖν αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: dramōn de tis kai gemisas spongon oxous peritheis kalamō epotizen auton, legōn· Aphete idōmen ei erchetai Ēlias kathelein auton.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus uttered a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἀφεὶς φωνὴν μεγάλην ἐξέπνευσεν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de Iēsous apheis phōnēn megalēn exepneusen.

paragraphs.text: And the veil of the temple was rent in two from the top to the bottom.
paragraphs.original: καὶ τὸ καταπέτασμα τοῦ ναοῦ ἐσχίσθη εἰς δύο ἀπʼ ἄνωθεν ἕως κάτω.
paragraphs.translit: kai to katapetasma tou naou eschisthē eis dyo apʼ anōthen heōs katō.

paragraphs.text: And when the centurion, who stood by over against him, saw that he so gave up the ghost, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God.
paragraphs.original: ἰδὼν δὲ ὁ κεντυρίων ὁ παρεστηκὼς ἐξ ἐναντίας αὐτοῦ ὅτι οὕτως ἐξέπνευσεν εἶπεν· Ἀληθῶς οὗτος ὁ ἄνθρωπος υἱὸς θεοῦ ἦν.
paragraphs.translit: idōn de ho kentyriōn ho parestēkōs ex enantias autou hoti houtōs exepneusen eipen· Alēthōs houtos ho anthrōpos hyios theou ēn.

paragraphs.text: And there were also women beholding from afar: among whom [were] both Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
paragraphs.original: Ἦσαν δὲ καὶ γυναῖκες ἀπὸ μακρόθεν θεωροῦσαι, ἐν αἷς καὶ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰακώβου τοῦ μικροῦ καὶ Ἰωσῆτος μήτηρ καὶ Σαλώμη,
paragraphs.translit: Ēsan de kai gynaikes apo makrothen theōrousai, en hais kai Maria hē Magdalēnē kai Maria hē Iakōbou tou mikrou kai Iōsētos mētēr kai Salōmē,

paragraphs.text: who, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and ministered unto him; and many other women that came up with him unto Jerusalem.
paragraphs.original: αἳ ὅτε ἦν ἐν τῇ Γαλιλαίᾳ ἠκολούθουν αὐτῷ καὶ διηκόνουν αὐτῷ, καὶ ἄλλαι πολλαὶ αἱ συναναβᾶσαι αὐτῷ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.
paragraphs.translit: hai hote ēn en tē Galilaia ēkolouthoun autō kai diēkonoun autō, kai allai pollai hai synanabasai autō eis Hierosolyma.

paragraphs.text: And when even was now come, because it was the Preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἤδη ὀψίας γενομένης, ἐπεὶ ἦν παρασκευή, ὅ ἐστιν προσάββατον,
paragraphs.translit: Kai ēdē opsias genomenēs, epei ēn paraskeuē, ho estin prosabbaton,

paragraphs.text: there came Joseph of Arimathaea, a councillor of honorable estate, who also himself was looking for the kingdom of God; and he boldly went in unto Pilate, and asked for the body of Jesus.
paragraphs.original: ἐλθὼν Ἰωσὴφ ὁ ἀπὸ Ἁριμαθαίας εὐσχήμων βουλευτής, ὃς καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν προσδεχόμενος τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ, τολμήσας εἰσῆλθεν πρὸς τὸν Πιλᾶτον καὶ ᾐτήσατο τὸ σῶμα τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: elthōn Iōsēph ho apo Harimathaias euschēmōn bouleutēs, hos kai autos ēn prosdechomenos tēn basileian tou theou, tolmēsas eisēlthen pros ton Pilaton kai ētēsato to sōma tou Iēsou.

paragraphs.text: And Pilate marvelled if he were already dead: and calling unto him the centurion, he asked him whether he had been any while dead.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ Πιλᾶτος ἐθαύμασεν εἰ ἤδη τέθνηκεν, καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος τὸν κεντυρίωνα ἐπηρώτησεν αὐτὸν εἰ πάλαι ἀπέθανεν·
paragraphs.translit: ho de Pilatos ethaumasen ei ēdē tethnēken, kai proskalesamenos ton kentyriōna epērōtēsen auton ei palai apethanen·

paragraphs.text: And when he learned it of the centurion, he granted the corpse to Joseph.
paragraphs.original: καὶ γνοὺς ἀπὸ τοῦ κεντυρίωνος ἐδωρήσατο τὸ πτῶμα τῷ Ἰωσήφ.
paragraphs.translit: kai gnous apo tou kentyriōnos edōrēsato to ptōma tō Iōsēph.

paragraphs.text: And he bought a linen cloth, and taking him down, wound him in the linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb which had been hewn out of a rock; and he rolled a stone against the door of the tomb.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀγοράσας σινδόνα καθελὼν αὐτὸν ἐνείλησεν τῇ σινδόνι καὶ ἔθηκεν αὐτὸν ἐν μνημείῳ ὃ ἦν λελατομημένον ἐκ πέτρας, καὶ προσεκύλισεν λίθον ἐπὶ τὴν θύραν τοῦ μνημείου.
paragraphs.translit: kai agorasas sindona kathelōn auton eneilēsen tē sindoni kai ethēken auton en mnēmeiō ho ēn lelatomēmenon ek petras, kai prosekylisen lithon epi tēn thyran tou mnēmeiou.

paragraphs.text: And Mary Magdalene and Mary the [mother] of Joses beheld where he was laid.
paragraphs.original: ἡ δὲ Μαρία ἡ Μαγδαληνὴ καὶ Μαρία ἡ Ἰωσῆτος ἐθεώρουν ποῦ τέθειται.
paragraphs.translit: hē de Maria hē Magdalēnē kai Maria hē Iōsētos etheōroun pou tetheitai.
